title: K-IR v0.2
description: Restructures kir-v0.1 around 8 universal objects (Symbol, Proposition, Context, Assertion, Evidence, Derivation, EpistemicStatus, RevisionEvent) instead of bolting fields onto the v0.1 Proposition. Scope is still exactly the 6 'particularly dangerous' cases from review (unknown concept/parent, unresolved truth, inconsistent evidence, concept split, previously-merged-must-separate, proof invalidation via retraction) PLUS two v0.1 STRESS_TEST.md gaps this shape fixes as a side effect: Finding 10 (functional vs set-valued predicates, via Symbol.functional) and part of Finding 6 (A implies B via Derivation, not a faked function symbol). Deliberately does NOT attempt: rich causality beyond simple composition, INFERENCE RULES for modal/belief/counterfactual/fictional contexts (the Context shape can now STORE a world/theory/frame key -- see 'context.world' example -- but nothing here defines what may or may not be inferred across a context boundary), numeric probability distributions, full bitemporal/versioned identity, or axiom-system-dependent proof checking. See CHANGELOG.md for why the shape changed mid-build.

Symbol.description: Everything referenceable is a Symbol: a concept/entity/type (kind=CONCEPT) or a relation/predicate (kind=RELATION). Relations being Symbols too means inventing a new predicate is adding a Symbol, not touching the schema -- and lets relation METADATA (functional vs set-valued) be attached and reasoned over generically instead of hand-derived per case (fixes v0.1 Finding 4/10).

resolution_status.description: Meaningful for kind=CONCEPT. RESOLVED: grounded, known parent or declared primitive. PROVISIONAL: created on ingestion, not yet checked against existing symbols. AMBIGUOUS: multiple candidate referents, see ambiguous_candidates. UNRESOLVED_PARENT: consistently named, but its supertype is not yet known. For kind=RELATION this field is typically RESOLVED once the relation's arity/functional-ness is declared, but may start PROVISIONAL for a relation invented on the fly.

parent.description: Symbol.id of the immediate supertype (CONCEPT) or a more general relation (RELATION), or null.

ambiguous_candidates.description: Only for resolution_status=AMBIGUOUS: candidate Symbol.ids this label might denote.

functional.description: kind=RELATION only. true: single-valued role (e.g. PrimaryMechanism) -- two Assertions of HOLDS(this(subject), differentValue) under the SAME Context are mechanically CONTRADICTS, no hand-labeling needed. false: set-valued role (e.g. Guarantees) -- differing values are NOT automatically contradictory. null: not yet classified (treat as unsafe to auto-derive from, per v0.1 Finding 10).

Term.description: A value-position argument. 'symbol_ref' points at a Symbol.id (a concept/entity). 'function' composes Symbols. No raw proposition-as-term here: embedding a full claim as an argument (belief/quotation, e.g. 'Alice believes P') stays out of scope -- represent A-implies-B relations via Derivation instead (see Derivation), which covers the material-implication case cleanly without faking a function symbol.

key.description: Open vocabulary, e.g. 'phase', 'regime', 'reference_frame', 'theory', 'world', 'software_version', 'observer'. New kinds of context need no schema change, only a new key -- this is the concrete fix for v0.1's fixed-field Context, which had no slot for 'world' or 'theory' and would have smuggled them into free-text assumptions (v0.1 Finding 7's problem, generalized).

constraints.description: Empty array = unconditional/universal context. NOTE (explicit correction): this generalizes STORAGE of any context key, including 'world' or 'theory'. It does NOT define which inferences are valid within or across a context boundary -- two propositions both true under world=Fiction do not compose the way two propositions under phase=liquid do. Cross-context inference rules are out of scope here (see description at schema root).

Proposition.description: Semantic content only -- no truth value, no confidence, no source. Those live in Assertion/Evidence/EpistemicStatus so a proposition's identity survives changing evidence.

predicate.description: A Symbol.id of kind=RELATION. (Still just a string reference, not a closed enum -- open-world extensible, but now at least points at a registered, inspectable Symbol instead of an arbitrary unvalidated string, partially closing v0.1 Finding 0.)

type.description: Symbol.id of the CONCEPT the variable ranges over.

Assertion.description: 'Source S claims proposition_id (with some stance)' -- kept separate from Evidence because a citation/interpretation (e.g. a paper's stated conclusion) is not the same kind of thing as a raw experimental result, and both need to coexist without corrupting each other (the BatchNorm ORIG/REVISED case: two papers ASSERT different mechanisms; that disagreement is about assertions, not about the propositions' truth).

stance.description: neutral_report: source states the proposition without taking an evidentiary stance on it (e.g. a survey paper repeating a claim).

Evidence.description: A specific empirical/derivational datum bearing on a proposition, distinct from an Assertion (a source's claim). Kept OUTSIDE the proposition so epistemic status is always a computed view.

status.description: active: counted toward epistemic status. retracted: source withdrawn, excluded from computation but never deleted. corrected: superseded by a newer Evidence object; old one kept for history.

independence_group.description: Evidence sharing a group id is NOT independent (e.g. reuses the same underlying dataset) -- future compiler work can down-weight non-independent evidence; not computed here.

derivation_ref.description: If kind=derivation_result: the Derivation.id this came from.

Derivation.description: Generalizes the ad-hoc hyperedges.json used in the physics/ML benchmarks into a first-class K-IR object, and gives v0.1 Finding 6's 'A implies B' case a home that isn't a faked function symbol: Differentiable(f) implies Continuous(f) becomes premises=[P_diff], conclusion=P_cont, rule='MaterialImplication', theory='RealAnalysis' -- no recursive proposition-as-term required for THIS shape of claim. (Propositional-attitude embedding, e.g. 'Alice believes P', is a different problem and stays deferred.)

relation.description: Open vocabulary, e.g. ENTAILS, COMPOSES_TO, GENERALIZES -- deliberately not a closed enum, same philosophy as predicate. COMPOSES_TO (e.g. Momentum+RMSProp -> Adam) is NOT claimed to be logical entailment; keeping this field open and separate from `rule` is what lets a real proof and an informal composition coexist in the same graph without one impersonating the other.

rule.description: The specific inference rule/justification, e.g. 'ClassicalConjunctionElimination', 'MaterialImplication', 'EmpiricalComposition'. Open string for now; a future tightening could make this a Symbol.id of kind RELATION, not done here.

theory.description: e.g. 'ClassicalLogic', 'RealAnalysis' -- the axiom/theory system the rule is valid under. Does not itself implement axiom-dependent proof checking (still deferred), just records the dependency.

context.description: Context.id, if the derivation only holds under some constraint (e.g. x != 0).

EpistemicStatus.description: A computed VIEW over a proposition's active Evidence, stored top-level (not embedded in Proposition) to make plain that this is derived data, recomputed whenever Evidence.status changes -- never hand-set, never treated as part of the proposition's identity.

status.description: Computed from ADMISSIBLE Evidence, where admissible means status=active AND (if kind=derivation_result) its referenced Derivation.status=valid. SUPPORTED: admissible evidence_for non-empty, evidence_against empty. REFUTED: reverse. UNRESOLVED: both empty. INCONSISTENT: both non-empty -- surfaced for investigation, never auto-resolved by picking a side. UNRESOLVED must never be treated as FALSE downstream. NOTE: the derivation-validity clause was added after validate_examples.py showed that an evidence-status-only rule cannot see a collapsed premise at all -- a retracted experiment leaves every downstream derived 'supporting' Evidence sitting at status=active, so the naive rule reports SUPPORTED forever. This clause makes one hop of invalidation detectable; chains deeper than one hop still require an explicit dependency-graph pass (not implemented).

proof_for.description: Derivation.id, if a certified derivation exists (stronger than evidence).

RevisionEvent.description: First-class, append-only operation log over Symbols/Propositions/Assertions/Evidence/Derivations. Concept split is ONE instance of this (operation=SPLIT), not a separate mechanism -- generalizing it means the same object also records CREATE/MERGE/SUPERSEDE/RETRACT/CORRECT/REFINE_CONTEXT/RETYPE_RELATION/INVALIDATE_PROOF/RESTORE, so 'we incorrectly merged two symbols and N facts now depend on it' has a place to be recorded and later reversed. This schema records the log entry; it does NOT implement an append-only storage engine or automatic downstream-dependency recomputation across arbitrary chains -- that remains compiler/storage-architecture future work.

reassignments.description: For operation=SPLIT/MERGE on target_kind=symbol: which propositions' argument references move to which resulting symbol id.
